title: Barger et al., Lancet Neurology 2014
finding: Orders of magnitude for in-flight sleep; used to set the simulated mean of about 6.5 h.

title: Otsuka et al., Scientific Reports 2021
finding: Sleep data in spaceflight; used with Barger 2014 to calibrate simulated sleep.

title: Norsk et al., Journal of Physiology 2015
finding: Heart rate and blood pressure in flight stay near pre-flight supine rest values; used to calibrate the simulated series.

title: NASA-STD-3001 Volume 1 (Rev C)
finding: Requirement V1 4031: protect crewmembers from the design reference solar particle event (the October 1989 events combined) to less than 250 mSv effective dose. It is a design target, not a personal dose limit. The 600 mSv career limit also comes from this standard (exact wording to be verified before citing).
link_or_doi: NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 1 Rev C, section 4.8.3, page 41: https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/nasa-std-3001-vol-1-rev-c-with-signature.pdf

title: NASA-STD-3001 Volume 2
finding: Reference for the oxygen-saturation alert limit. Exact wording to be verified before citing.
link_or_doi: NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 2 (exact wording to be verified before citing)

title: Zeitlin et al., Science 340:1080 (2013)
finding: Dose-equivalent rate measured on the way to Mars (MSL RAD), about 1.8 mSv/day; used for the simulated transit rate.
link_or_doi: Science 340:1080 (DOI to be confirmed before showing it on screen)

title: Guo et al., Astronomy & Astrophysics 2015
finding: Solar particle events add a small share of the transit dose; used for the simulated storm spikes (about 5% of the total).

title: Stahn et al., Scientific Reports 2017
finding: Reference for body temperature in spaceflight. The 38.0 °C fever limit is our own design rule.

title: Lang et al., Journal of Bone and Mineral Research 2004
finding: Reference for bone loss in spaceflight (Bones and muscle zone). Confirm before citing.
link_or_doi: J Bone Miner Res 2004 (DOI to be confirmed)

title: Battelino et al., 2019 (Earth reference)
finding: Earth consensus range for glucose targets (70 to 180 mg/dL). Not validated for spaceflight.

title: Gew et al., Eye 2026
finding: Reference for the vision self-check (spaceflight-associated neuro-ocular syndrome). Confirm citation before showing it.

title: Design rule (our own design, not NASA's)
finding: Thresholds chosen by the team for this demo. Decision support only.
used_for: mood, fluids, exercise, symptoms, glucose, temp
